$comment: Rust tier. Files permitted to disable MockProvider broadcast validation (MockProvider::always_ack / disable_broadcast_validation() / enable_broadcast_validation(false)). See docs/audit/2026-08-testing-gap-remediation-plan.md Phase A5 and packages/runar-rs/README.md 'How fund-path tests fail closed in the Rust tier'. Fund-path deploy/call tests with a real LocalSigner and a real compiled contract MUST NOT appear here.

entries.reason: Directly tests the opt-out surface itself (MockProvider::always_ack, disable_broadcast_validation, enable_broadcast_validation(false)) so those escape hatches keep working. Every other test in the file uses the default validating provider, including a real LocalSigner deploy fund path.

8 of ~120 inline #[cfg(test)] tests (deploy_broadcasts_transaction, deploy_tracks_utxo_for_call, call_fails_unknown_method, call_fails_wrong_arg_count and the four terminal_call_* tests) drive a synthetic make_artifact("51", ...) OP_TRUE contract with MockSigner, whose signatures are placeholders no OP_CHECKSIG can verify. They assert SDK wiring — UTXO tracking, arg validation, terminal output shape — not spendability. Every other test in the file uses the default validating provider.
Synthetic OP_TRUE artifact signed by MockSigner; the tests assert unlocking-script WIRE BYTES (auto-injected witness param filtering, prevOutScript/serialisedOutputs ordering), not spendability.

Synthetic OP_TRUE artifact signed by MockSigner; asserts that a nil ByteString arg is rejected at build time with the offending parameter named. The deploy step is setup, not the assertion under test.
Synthetic oversized/OP_TRUE artifacts signed by MockSigner; asserts the SDK's own MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES guard fires. The transactions are deliberately pathological in size, not spendable.
Synthetic OP_TRUE artifact signed by MockSigner; asserts the coin-selection algorithm's input COUNT and the maxFundingInputs cap error, not script validity of the resulting transaction.
